tools.name: search_providers
tools.description: Search Gigstereo's marketplace of event providers in Colombia (DJs, mariachis, photographers, videographers, bands, decorators, catering…) by city and, optionally, service or name. Owner-verified profiles show a price range and reviews; unclaimed directory listings show neither. Link the user to eac

tools.name: get_provider
tools.description: Public profile of one provider by its slug (the last part of its profileUrl): description, city, service radius, price range and rating when the profile is owner-verified.

tools.name: get_price_guide
tools.description: Reference prices Gigstereo publishes for a service in a city, each with its source and the date it was checked, plus the city page (cityPageUrl) that shows them. The only reliable source of price figures here: never invent prices. Cite cityPageUrl when you quote them. Final prices are quoted by each

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Gigstereo's service categories (Spanish names with their slugs) and the Colombian cities that have a city page. Optional: search_providers and request_quotes also understand plain service names.

tools.name: request_quotes
tools.description: Send the user's event request to matching providers on Gigstereo, for free: the providers who are interested contact the user directly by WhatsApp or email with their price. It is not a booking and costs nothing. Before calling: (1) collect the details from the user — never invent a name, phone or e

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_quotes" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Send the user's event request to matching providers on Gigstereo, for free: the providers who are interested contact the user directly by WhatsApp or email with…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_providers · Private data: request_quotes · Public sink: request_quotes.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_providers · Private data: request_quotes · Public sink: request_quotes

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
